text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.22% today in a flat-to-down session, even as oil prices spiked to six-week highs on escalating Middle East tensions—Iran's Houthi allies attacked Saudi energy facilities, pushing Brent crude above $98 a barrel. For an oil producer, this should typically be a tailwind, but the stock gave back most of yesterday's $1.48 jump, suggesting investors may have already priced in the supply-shock premium over the past few trading days.

The broader move higher over the past two weeks (+0.91%) aligns with the oil price climb and geopolitical anxiety in the region, which tends to support commodity-linked equities. However, today's muted reaction despite the news headlines hints that markets may be weighing competing factors—perhaps caution about how sustained these tensions will remain, or how quickly they could de-escalate.
